X.}}</noinclude>things that you heare, and heard them not. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=25}}† And behold a certaine lavvyer stoode vp, tempting him and saying, Maister, by doing of what thing shal I possesse life euerlasting? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=26}}† But he said to him, In the lavv vvhat is vvritten? hovv readest thou? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=27}}† He ansvvering said, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Deu. 6, 5.''}}* ''Thou shalt loue the Lord thy God vvith thy whole hart, and vvith thy whole soule, and vvith al thy strength, and vvith al thy minde: and thy neighbour as thy self''.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lev. 19, 18.''}} {{verse|chapter=10|verse=28}}† And he said to him, Thou hast ansvvered right, {{sup|‖}} this doe and thou shalt liue. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=29}}† But he desirous to iustifie him self, said to {{sc|Iesvs}}, And vvho is my neighbour? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=30}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} taking it, said, A certaine man vvent dovvne from Hierusalem into Iericho, and fel among theeues, vvho also spoiled him, and giuing him vvoundes vvent avvay leauing him {{sup|‖}} halfe-dead. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=31}}† And it chaunced that a certaine Priest vvent dovvne the same vvay: and seeing him, passed by. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=32}}† In like maner also a Leuite, vvhen he vvas neere the place, and savv him, passed by. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=33}}† But a certaine Samaritane going his iourney, came neere him: and seeing him, vvas moued vvith mercie. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=34}}† And going vnto him, bound his vvoundes, povvring in oile and vvine: and setting him vpon his ovvne beast, brought him into an inne, and tooke care of him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=35}}† And the next day he tooke forth two pence, and gaue to the host, and said, Haue care of him: and vvhatsoeuer thou shalt {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ S. Augustin saith that the Apostle ''(1. Cor. 9''.) according to this place did supererogate, that is, did more then he needed or was bound to doe, vvhen he might haue required al duties for preaching the Gospel, but would not. ''li. de op. Monach. c. 5''. whereof it commeth, that the workes vvhich we doe more then precept, be called workes of Supererogation: & whereby it is also euident against the Protestants, that there be such workes. See Optatus li. 6 cont. Parmen. how aptly he applyeth this parable to S. Paules counsel of virginitie (1 Cor. 7) as to a worke of supererogation.}}∷ {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''Supererogaveris, προσδαπανήσῃς,''}}∷ supererogate, I at my returne vvil repay thee. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=36}}† Vvhich of these three in thy opinion vvas neighbour to him that fel among theeues? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=37}}† But he said, He that did mercie vpon him. And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, Goe, and doe thou in like maner.⊣ {{verse|chapter=10|verse=38}}† b {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=b The Gospel vpon the Assumptiō of our Lady ''Aug. 15.''}}And it came to passe as they vvent, and he entred into a certaine tovvne: and a certaine vvoman named Martha, receiued him into her house, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=39}}† and she had a sister called Marie. vvho sitting also at our Lords feete, heard his vvord. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=40}}† But Martha vvas busie about much seruice. vvho stoode and said, Lord, hast thou no care that my sister hath left me alone to serue? speake to her therfore, that she help me. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=41}}† And our Lord ansvvering said to her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful, and art troubled about very many things. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=42}}† But one thing is necessarie. {{sup|‖}} Marie hath chosen the best part vvhich shal not be taken avvay from her.⊣
